day.headline: Big bank results: ICICI and Axis strong, HDFC Bank slow; markets react on Monday
day.summary: Three of the most widely held stocks in Indian equity funds reported Q2 on Saturday. ICICI Bank's bad loans fell to multi-year lows, Axis Bank's profit jumped 38%, and HDFC Bank grew profit under 5%. See Monday 19/10 for how the market reacted.

items.title: ICICI Bank Q2: profit up 20% to ₹14,843 cr; gross bad loans down to 1.20%
items.why: ICICI Bank is among the largest holdings across equity funds, and it was the stock managers sold most in September (−₹2,614 cr). Margin slipped to 4.18%, but asset quality keeps improving.

items.title: HDFC Bank Q2: profit up 4.7% to ₹19,510 cr (headline figures)
items.why: Slow growth continues at India's biggest bank. Fund managers were net buyers in September (+₹2,145 cr, 67 funds adding), so its share-price reaction matters for most large-cap and flexi-cap portfolios.

items.title: Axis Bank Q2: profit up 38% to ₹7,003 cr; margin at 3.36% (headline figures)
items.why: In line with the 37–43% growth analysts expected. The margin dip was expected because of costlier foreign-currency deposits.

items.title: Fund houses turn more positive on large caps as valuations ease
items.why: Useful context when clients ask whether to keep investing: SBI MF says large-cap sentiment is 'deeply pessimistic' (often a contrarian buy signal) and Nifty's three-year return has fallen to 6% a year, a post-2020 low. ICICI Pru's equity valuation indicator is at 99.9, just short of its 'invest in equities' zone, and HDFC Balanced Advantage held over 73% net equity in September.

items.title: PSU banks rally on Q2: Union Bank profit +30.3% to ₹5,537 cr; PNB up to 7.7%
items.why: While private banks fell, public sector banks gained on results, helping PSU and value-oriented funds. Union Bank rose up to 4.9% and PNB (net interest income +10.8%) up to 7.7% on Monday morning.
